incident-bot: PAGING: auth-header-beacon detected from multiple edge IPs — suspicious repeated Authorization header fragments in logs. Severity: high. Auto-created incident INC-2026-1002. Link: https://incidents.local/INC-2026-1002

olivia: seeing the same spike in edge-proxy metrics, ~350 req/s with Authorization pattern. Most requests to /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.

sanjay: tagging sec @marta and oncall @eli. Any immediate customer impact?

marta: quick check — backend 200s largely intact but we have a rising 401 rate for a subset of tokens. Could be token replay or leaked fragments forwarded in logs. Need to preserve artifacts.

olivia: pasted a few sanitized lines: ```
edge-proxy[proxy-7] 2026-03-18T12:02:41Z GET /v1/generate 200 "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...XYZfrag"
edge-proxy[proxy-7] 2026-03-18T12:02:41Z POST /v1/embeddings 401 "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...XYZfrag"
```

eli: I will take owner for live mitigation. Plan: 1) contain suspicious IPs at WAF 2) rotate service tokens for suspected svc accounts 3) preserve logs to secure bucket.

marta: agree. suspected svc accounts: svc-ingest-front, svc-telemetry-shipper. Also check any recently changed log-forwarder configs that might have leaked headers.

sanjay: I'm opening INC ticket and pinging CS for customer outreach. INC-2026-1002 created. Attaching initial timeline and affected customers list (partial).

legal-bot: Legal notified. If PII exposure is suspected, do not delete artifacts; move to secure preserve path: s3://redwood-incident-preserve/INC-2026-1002 and set retention to locked.

olivia: starting targeted grep and preserve: `grep -R "Authorization: Bearer" /var/log/edge-proxy/ | gzip > /tmp/auth-frags.gz` then `aws s3 cp /tmp/auth-frags.gz s3://redwood-incident-preserve/INC-2026-1002/` (doing in a sanitized environment).

eli: containment actions done: WAF rules added to block 3 IP ranges (1.2.3.0/24, 5.6.7.8/32, 9.10.11.0/24). Token rotation commands queued.

marta: verify metrics and confirm no uptick in error rate for premium customers; we should enable model-fallback routing for affected routes to avoid degrading experience.

sanjay: CS notified 3 enterprise customers with brief: "we detected anomalous auth header activity; we're rotating service tokens and preserving logs; no confirmed data exfiltration; will follow up."

eli: starting forced rotation: `rbacctl rotate-token --service svc-ingest-front --force` then `rbacctl rotate-token --service svc-telemetry-shipper --force`. ETA ~20m.

olivia: monitoring — auth 401 spike dropping after WAF blocks. Some residual requests from other IPs, continuing to scrub.

marta: check forwarding pipeline configs: found one log-forwarder with header_includes: ["Authorization"] by mistake in staging -> rotated and patched. Verify prod configs too.

sanjay: documenting handoff: night oncall @tess to complete rotation and confirm KMS key swap for rotated tokens. Handoff ETA 13:00 UTC.

tess: ack. I'll take over for the rotation sweep, confirm revocations, and validate that no valid customer tokens were impacted.

eli: summary for the bridge: severity=high, suspected exposure of token fragments in logs, containment in progress, rotation underway, customers notified. Owner -> eli, next oncall -> tess. Preserved artifacts -> s3://redwood-incident-preserve/INC-2026-1002.
